Edge-IIoT traffic and communication patterns change over time, shifting the load across connected devices and servers.
Traffic datasets record what happened, but not the latency, energy or delivery outcomes of routing actions that were never taken.
Represent the network as a graph, learn a routing policy, and screen candidate actions with a structural model before execution.
Can graph-aware learning and counterfactual screening improve routing performance and explainability under changing traffic?

This is the problem statement derived from the user-supplied project brief. The dataset has no recorded outcomes for the six alternative routing actions, so this implementation evaluates decisions in a synthetic three-server simulator. Latency and energy are proxies. The proposed learned action-aware SCM remains a research aspiration; the current Phase 5 screen is an exact SCM of the simulator.
Edge-IIoTset (primary) or TON_IoT; graph nodes represent devices or edge servers, with communication/dependency links.
NOTEARS, DirectLiNGAM or PC for a candidate causal structure; refine using domain knowledge.
GNN graph embedding with a PPO or DQN agent; evaluate alternative actions with an SCM before execution.
Latency, energy, throughput, PDR, task completion, reward, distribution-shift robustness and explanation fidelity.
Implemented variant: Edge-IIoTset, observed endpoints, NOTEARS, GATv2, DQN and exact simulator SCM.

This slide records the supplied problem scope separately from the actual implemented choices. TON_IoT, DirectLiNGAM, PC and PPO are alternatives, not runs in this repository. Observed IP endpoints are used as graph nodes without validated device/server roles. The Phase 2 learned linear SCM is observational. The Phase 5 action-aware SCM is an independent exact model of the simulator; it is not learned from the Phase 2 DAG.
